title: 7.10 An 8-to-28GHz 8-Phase Clock Generator Using Dual-Feedback Ring Oscillator in 28nm CMOS
problem: Multi-phase clock generation for high-speed wireline transceivers (>224Gb/s PAM-4) requires low jitter and phase error across wide frequency range (8–28GHz); PLL-based approaches become costly at fT limits of 200–300GHz CMOS processes.
motivation: As fT approaches practical limits, PLL + high-N divider topology becomes infeasible for generating multi-phase clocks; DLL approaches suffer phase error accumulation; ring-oscillator injection-locking offers better feedback but limited to fT/2 operation.
method: The circuit uses two feedback loops working together: a delay-locked loop (a timing-synchronization circuit that creates eight aligned clock phases from a single input) and a ring oscillator (an oscillator made from chained inverters that pulse back and forth) that locks onto these phases and reinforces them. The ring oscillator's internal feedback simultaneously reduces jitter (small unwanted timing variations) and phase error (misalignment between intended and actual clock timing) across the wide 8–28GHz frequency range. This dual-feedback approach achieves the low jitter and accurate timing needed for high-speed data transmission without requiring the expensive divider circuits that traditional phase-locked loops need.
key_novelty: The core innovation combines a delay-locked loop with a ring oscillator's self-regulating feedback to achieve both low timing error and low jitter across 8–28GHz without needing the expensive dividers of traditional phase-locked loops.
contributions: 8-phase clock generation from 8–28GHz with low jitter and phase error
Avoids PLL-divider topology infeasible at fT saturation
Ring oscillator feedback suppresses phase error vs. standalone DLL chains
Suitable for 224Gb/s PAM-4 and higher-rate transceivers
